narrative:
The model determined that you have a 56% chance of being a bad credit risk. Because this probability is above the approval threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were your credit history, the status of your checking account, and your installment rate as a percentage of disposable income. Your credit history of having all prior loans paid back at this bank was the single biggest driver pushing the prediction toward bad credit risk. Although this sounds positive, in the data this particular history is very rare among approved applicants (only 2.9% of successful cases) and the model treats it as a warning sign compared with the far more common “existing credits paid on time” profile of approved borrowers. 

The status of your checking account (currently in negative balance) was the second strongest factor and also pulled the prediction toward denial. Most approved applicants (59%) have no checking account or a positive balance, making your negative status stand out unfavorably.

Your requested installment rate worked in your favor: at only 1% of your disposable income it is well below the 3% average of approved loans and therefore pushed the prediction slightly toward approval. Unfortunately, this positive signal was not strong enough to overcome the negative impact of the other two dominant factors.

You should focus on building a more typical positive credit history with this bank, bring your checking account balance above zero, and then reapply. These steps address the exact issues the model weighed most heavily. (248 words)
